MIND. [1] [Carbn. s.]
Difficult thinking, memory weakened.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Carbn. s.]
Vertigo, sudden attacks, while sitting.
Dull muddled feeling in forehead ; as if contracting.
Confusion. θ Headache.
Drunken, unconscious from whisky.
Asphyxia. See 26.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Carbn. s.]
Pressure, most in forehead.
Violent headache, increasing till mind is affected.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Carbn. s.]
Dim sight ; objects fade away.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Carbn. s.]
Stitches in ears ; after stool.
   

TEETH AND GUMS. [10] [Carbn. s.]
Toothache brought on by warm food.
Neuralgia of teeth.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Carbn. s.]
Saltish taste of phlegm hawked up from fauces.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Carbn. s.]
Sour belching and passage of much sour flatus ; > from belching.
Vomiting of bitter water.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Carbn. s.]
Pressure in region of stomach and under sternum, with herpetic dyscrasia.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Carbn. s.]
Liver complaint, with dropsical swelling of feet.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Carbn. s.]
Cutting pains in bowels.
Rumbling and flatulent complaints ; twisting, rolling, and rumbling as if diarrhœa would set in.
Fulness and distension of abdomen.
Strangulated hernia.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Carbn. s.]
Chronic diarrhœa, which set in every four to six weeks and lasted for one or two days ; yellowish, frothy, sour smelling fluid evacuations, with tenesmus and colicky pains, particularly in umbilical region, through which the navel was drawn inward ; came on during night.
Stool not increased, but accompanied by tenesmus.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Carbn. s.]
Labor-pains too weak.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Carbn. s.]
Expiration hot ; breathing difficult ; flying stitches and burning in chest ; quickly passing over ; but frequently returning.
Asphyxia from alcohol and from coal gas.
   

INNER CHEST AND LUNGS. [28] [Carbn. s.]
Flying-burning and stitches in chest. θ Phthisis.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Carbn. s.]
Spasmodic pulse. θ Headache.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Carbn. s.]
Goitre.
   

UPPER LIMBS. [32] [Carbn. s.]
Crackling in right shoulder joint from every motion, connected with more or less severe stitches from shoulder joint to elbow, with every change of weather.
Stitches from shoulder joint to elbow, or even to wrist, especially violent after midnight and during damp or cold weather.
Wrist joint scalded with boiling water ; wrist much swollen, blisters partially opened.
Slight scald of left hand ; bright redness without much pain or swelling.
Gout of hand.
Herpes phlyctænoides, covering dorsal surface of hand.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Carbn. s.]
Jerking, stitching rheumatic pains in lower limbs.
Chronic sciatica in right thigh, movements of limb impeded.
Impetigo : pimples which form scabs, in the popliteal space and on dorsum of foot and hand.
Cold feet.
Rheumatism of lower extremities ; slightest motion brings on violent pains, particularly in hips and knees, with redness and swelling of feet.
   

LIMBS IN GENERAL. [34] [Carbn. s.]
Tearing in all limbs, coming and going, now in one and again in another limb.
Tearing in limbs, with herpes of face.
Jerking, stitching, tearing, flying pains, returning at regular intervals, for a long time.
Crackling of joints after previous gouty affections of joints.
Chronic rheumatic and arthritic affections.
   

FEVER. [40] [Carbn. s.]
Feverish attacks. θ Headache.
Coldness. θ Headache.
   

ATTACKS, PERIODICITY. [41] [Carbn. s.]
Short but quickly returning attacks, at regular intervals.
   

TISSUES. [44] [Carbn. s.]
Enlarged and indurated lymphatic glands.
Cold swellings.
Rheumatic troubles.
Rheumatism, either without fever or with only slight fever.
Rheumatism and gout ; after the relief of acute and inflammatory conditions.
Chronic rheumatic and arthritic affections, which, of themselves, are without fever.
Gout, but not gouty dyscrasia.
Gouty swellings when not of too long standing.
Tuberculosis of lungs or bowels.
   

TOUCH. PASSIVE MOTION. INJURIES. [45] [Carbn. s.]
Scalds and burns.
   

SKIN. [46] [Carbn. s.]
Itch and herpetic affections.
Vesicles on a red, inflamed and swollen base, partly close together, but mostly separated ; they contain an opaque, yellowish fluid, which forms thick, yellowish scabs, sometimes the discharge excoriates and produces violent itching. θ Herpes phlyctænoides.
Pimples which form scabs, in popliteal space and on dorsum of foot and hands. θ Impetigo.
